metadata.subject: Algorithms
metadata.title: Discover Depth-First Search
metadata.description: Explore one graph branch deeply, then backtrack to the next path.

learning_objectives: Track the DFS stack/path and visited nodes.
Recognize backtracking when a branch ends.

mission.title: Go deep, then backtrack
mission.description: Follow one branch as far as it goes before returning to another waiting node.

introduction.title: DFS explores one branch deeply
introduction.content: Depth-First Search (DFS) follows a path as far as possible before it backtracks and tries another branch.
points: A graph is made of nodes and connections.
The stack or path remembers where to return.

visual.visual: A → B → D, then backtrack → E → C

worked_example.title: Go deep before turning back
worked_example.content: Starting at A, DFS follows B before visiting C.

steps.explanation: A is visited first; its neighbors become waiting choices.

steps.visual: Visited: A → B | Stack/path: C → D → E
steps.explanation: DFS chooses B and pushes its neighbors, going deeper before C.

steps.visual: Visited: A → B → D | backtrack to B
steps.explanation: D has no unvisited neighbors, so DFS returns to the most recent unfinished branch.

worked_example.conclusion: DFS may reach a far node before a nearby branch because depth comes before breadth.

next.title: Now explore the graph.
next.content: Watch the current path and backtracking state.

next-step: A is the starting node, so DFS visits it first.
The current path chooses the next deepest branch.
A leaf has no new neighbors, so DFS backtracks.
DFS has visited every reachable node.

prediction.heading: After visiting A…
prediction.question: Which node will DFS follow next?
prediction.selection_message: Your prediction: {prediction}. Continue DFS to check it.
prediction.required_message: Choose the next node DFS will follow.

result.actual: DFS follows {actual} next along the current path.

actions.label: Visit the start node
actions.task: Choose the start node and begin the current path.

actions.label: Follow the first branch
actions.task: Choose the deepest available neighbor on the path.

actions.label: Backtrack from a leaf
actions.task: When a branch ends, return to the newest unfinished choice.

actions.label: Explore the next branch
actions.task: Choose the next node from the current stack-like path.

actions.label: Complete the traversal
actions.task: Continue until every reachable node is visited.

challenge.title: DFS challenge
challenge.start_message: Traverse from A by following a branch deeply before backtracking.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Replay DFS by choosing the next deep node.

phases.title: Visit every node
phases.instruction: Choose each node in depth-first order by following the current path and backtracking at leaves.
phases.feedback: Follow the current path deeply; backtrack only when the branch has no new neighbor.

guidance.start_message: Choose the next node at the top of the DFS path.

items.content: From A, follow B before returning to C.

phases.title: Practise the DFS path
phases.instruction: Select and confirm the deepest available node, then backtrack.
phases.feedback: The top of the path is the next node; a leaf makes DFS backtrack.

phases.title: Apply DFS
phases.instruction: Traverse the new graph by following one branch deeply.
phases.feedback: When a branch ends, backtrack to the newest unfinished choice.

phases.title: Solve DFS
phases.instruction: Reach every node in the deterministic depth-first order.
phases.feedback: Go to the deepest available neighbor before choosing a different branch.

guidance.start_message: Master depth-first traversal on this unfamiliar graph.

phases.title: Master DFS
phases.instruction: Predict and confirm each deep visit and backtrack.
phases.feedback: DFS follows a branch until it must backtrack.

thinking.title: Predict the DFS path
thinking.instruction: Mentally follow the stack/path and predict visits and backtracking.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not click the graph yet. Follow the deepest available branch.

prediction_fields.label: Visit order
prediction_fields.prompt: Which nodes will DFS visit, in order?

feedback.all_correct: You predicted the path and backtracking.
feedback.incorrect: Follow the deepest unvisited neighbor, then backtrack when a branch ends.

solve.title: Expert DFS
solve.instruction: Traverse the generated graph with no hints.
solve.perfect_result: You followed the path and backtracked at the right moments.

quiz.question: What does DFS do when a branch has no unvisited neighbor?

discovery.title: DFS discovery
discovery.summary: DFS uses a stack-like path to go deep into one branch before backtracking to another choice.

sections.title: What?
sections.content: DFS explores one branch of a graph as deeply as possible before backtracking.

sections.title: Example
sections.content: From A, visit B, then D; when D ends, return and continue with E or C.

sections.title: Why?
sections.content: A stack or recursion path remembers where to return after a branch finishes.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: Go deep → reach a dead end → backtrack → try the next branch.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of a maze
alternate_explanations.content: Walk down one hallway until it ends, then walk back to the last junction and try another.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through it
alternate_explanations.content: A → B → D, backtrack to B → E, then backtrack to A → C.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why does DFS backtrack?
recall.model_answer: DFS backtracks when the current branch has no unvisited neighbor, returning to the most recent earlier node with another choice.
